newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks ride futures to higher close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks ride futures to higher close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2439 +36 US 30yr cl 6.71 -0.03
10yrbond futs 92.675 +0.040 Gold NY 344.25 Lon fix 346.30
*Stocks fly home to higher close, lifted by futures-led buying and bargain hunters. Volume 361.12 million, value A$696.11 million, 1,130 stocks traded, 476 steady, 311 up, 343 down.
The Australian share market flew home to a higher finish on Wednesday, lifted by futures-led buying interest and value seeking investors who saw Tuesday's selloff as overdone.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 26.7 points at 2,435.8. March share price index futures were 36 points higher at 2,439, a 3.2 point premium to the index.

Despite the non-arrival of a widely expected easing in official interest rates, interest on the buy side was enough to see the benchmark more than recoup all of Tuesday's losses and end near its highs for the day.

"There has been solid interest on the buy side for most of the day," said a Sydney broker, pointing to the return of the March SPI future contract to a modest premium after trading at a discount for several weeks.
"Futures generated a lot of the interest, especially in BHP."
BHP added over two percent to close at A$17.78, recovering all of its losses in Tuesday's overdone selling and fractionally firmer than Monday's close.
Other rises were generally widespread, with the miners having slightly the better of it on the day.
At the smaller end, transaction technology developer Intellect Holdings jumped to two year high of A$1.15 as traders voted their approval of recent contracts awarded to the group.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was substantial as traders reset positions with the March SPI contract moving back to a premium. Options trade was reasonably active.
Total options traded 38,808 (30,287). Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 9,669 (8,283).
In other local markets, domestic buying helped Australian bond yields to close slightly lower and saw the market recover from an early set-back after the Reserve Bank failed to ease.
By 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.27 percent, down from Tuesday's 7.33 percent.
The Australian dollar subsided to a soft close as the market found the Reserve Bank's silence an uncomfortable one.
Many traders remained concerned that a cut in interest rates was still a possibility despite the absence of such an easing today.
By 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT), the local dollar had softened to US$0.7624/29, having briefly touching US$0.7650 when it became clear the RBA would not be moving on rates today.
